title: Cutoff for the Overhand Shuffle
summary: We study the overhand shuffle with a fixed cut probability $p\in(0,1)$. In the packet-reversal convention, each gap is cut independently with probability $p$, and each resulting packet is reversed in place. We prove total-variation cutoff at \[ \frac{p^2}{2(1-p)π^2}\,n^2\log n. \] The lower bound uses an exact finite-deck cosine eigenfunction and a uniform conditional-variance estimate. For the upper bound, a coalescing coupling reduces a transposition discrepancy to a symmetric killed two-card chain. Its principal decay rate is $(1-p)π^2/(p^2n^2)+o(n^{-2})$.
